subject: Clarify finance archival for account usage records vs customer data erasure
messages:
From: Billie Chen <billie@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on invoice/usage data retention when requesting deletion

Hi Karthik,

Quick question from our security/compliance team: if we submit a data deletion request for our users, what happens to the usage records and invoices tied to our account? Our finance team needs copies of invoices for audit purposes and we want to make sure a deletion request from our org won't remove records they legally need to keep. Can you confirm Redwood's position and any exceptions for accounting/legal retention?

Thanks,
Billie Chen
Director of Security & Compliance
Acme Corp


From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Billie Chen <billie@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on invoice/usage data retention when requesting deletion

Hi Billie,

Thanks for raising this — important and a common ask. Looping in Laura (Finance) and Marissa (Billing) so they can confirm the exact retention windows and legal / accounting exceptions. A couple of quick clarifying points from our side:

- When customers request account-level erasure, we differentiate between transactional/financial records (invoices, payment receipts, billing ledger entries) and user-level content or raw usage logs that may contain customer data.
- For accounting and tax reasons, certain financial records are retained for a statutory period. We want to confirm how that applies in your jurisdiction and whether Acme requires extracts before erasure.

Laura / Marissa — can you confirm Redwood's retention policy for invoices and associated usage records (preferred retention term, whether we can provide redacted extracts, and the process to mark records as retained for legal reasons)? Also attaching our internal summary for reference.

Next step: Laura — if you can provide the canonical retention length and whether we can produce an audit bundle for Acme to satisfy auditors, I'll relay that back to Billie with proposed timing.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RetentionPolicy_Summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on invoice/usage data retention when requesting deletion

Karthik / Marissa,

Providing the finance view here. Summary below — happy to join a call with Acme if helpful.

- Invoices & payment receipts: retained for 7 years by default to support accounting, tax, and audit requirements (this aligns with our standard corporate record retention policy). These are transactional records and are considered accounting records; they are not deleted on a standard customer erasure request unless there is a legally binding requirement to do so (e.g., court order).
- Billing ledger entries / invoice line items: retained alongside invoices for the same period. We can provide PDF copies and CSV exports of invoice history on request.
- Raw per-request usage logs (request payloads, prompt text): treated as user data. Customers may request erasure of those logs. When erasure is requested, we remove raw logs from hot storage and schedule it for deletion from long-term backups in accordance with our deletion SLA and backup retention windows.
- Aggregated billing metrics / metered totals: we keep aggregated usage metrics for billing reconciliation and product analytics. These are retained in pseudonymized/aggregated form and are not tied to raw PII.

Acme-specific options we can offer:
- Provide an "audit bundle" containing invoice PDFs and a CSV ledger (redacted for any PII in line items) before we execute an erasure for user-level logs.
- Flag transactional records as "retained for legal/accounting" so they are not removed by an erasure workflow; we can record the legal basis and retention reason.

I've attached the retention table with statutory notes by jurisdiction and a short summary doc you can share with Acme. If they need evidence (SOC2 export, invoice PDFs), we can deliver within 3 business days after request.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Accounting_Retention_Table.xlsx (xlsx); RetentionPolicy_Summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Billie Chen <billie@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on invoice/usage data retention when requesting deletion

Hi Billie — thanks for the patience. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

Recap:
- Invoices and billing records are retained for 7 years by Redwood for accounting and legal compliance. Those are considered transactional records and will not be deleted as part of a standard customer erasure request unless compelled by law.
- Raw request-level logs (which may include prompt text or user content) are removable per your erasure request; we will delete them from primary and schedule removal from backups per our backup retention policy.
- Aggregated usage metrics used for billing/analytics are kept in pseudonymized form and are not reversible to user content.

What we can do for Acme right now:
1) Produce an audit bundle (invoice PDFs + redacted ledger CSV) and deliver via secure Share link within 3 business days.
2) If you want transactional records flagged as retained for legal reasons on our side, confirm the legal basis and we will record it as part of the retention metadata.
3) Execute an erasure request for raw logs once you confirm the scope (all user request logs up to date X).

Please reply with which of the options you want (1/2/3) and we'll schedule delivery. Happy to join a short call if that helps.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
